segments.t: Tied up together in a basement, Denis and Nikita bicker over Nikita's cowardly scheme. Fortunately for them, the lead kidnapper gets a phone call from his visiting mother and postpones dealing with them until after a sightseeing trip, leaving a single guard.
Не мог выйти один на один?
Не хотел об тебя руки марать.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.

'Well, is this a very unexpected twist?' Asking whether this a very unexpected twist cuts straight through the tension between Denis and the guest. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
'Oh, just shut up right now!' Nikita insists that just shut up right now, leaving Denis no room to argue.
'Hello, Mom, hi, we are working.' The guest mentions that Mom hi they are working so Denis sees what is at stake.
'Yes, of course, we will meet as we agreed.' Claiming that they will meet as they agreed sounds confident, even if Denis has doubts.
Не мог выйти один на один?
'Could you not face me one on one?' Checking whether the guest not face him one on one cuts straight through the tension between Denis and the guest.
Не хотел об тебя руки марать.

'I did not want to dirty my hands on you.' Saying that he did not want to dirty his hands on Denis is how Nikita sets the tone with Denis. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'You are to blame for everything yourself!' Once the guest is to blame for everything themselves, Denis makes sure the guest hears every word. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
'Well, have you calmed down now?' By checking whether Denis calmed down now, the guest presses Denis for a straight answer.

'Your business is postponed for a little while.' Even though Denis's business is postponed for a little, the guest keeps a steady face in front of Denis. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.

'You are staying here to guard these two.' Admitting that Denis is staying here to guard these two shows the guest being honest for a change. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
'And we will drive back here soon.' Saying that they will drive back here soon is how the guest sets the tone with Denis.

'We need to get out of here urgently.' By needing to get out of here urgently, Denis keeps his side of the story grounded. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Не мог выйти один на один?
Не хотел об тебя руки марать.
While Denis and Nikita look for a way to overpower their lone guard, Nastya carries out her secret DNA mission at home. Until next time!
